bottom_line: MiCA full application creates first comprehensive crypto regulatory framework in a major jurisdiction; non-EU exchanges must obtain authorization to serve EU clients.
what_changed: Full MiCA provisions entered into force, requiring all crypto-asset service providers operating in the EU to obtain authorization from a national competent authority.
why_it_matters: Creates licensing barrier for non-EU exchanges; stablecoin issuers face reserve and redemption requirements; institutional adoption path clarified.
main_uncertainty: National competent authority capacity to process applications varies; grandfathering provisions differ by member state.

scenarios.name: Orderly transition
scenarios.description: Major exchanges obtain licenses; market consolidates around compliant players.

scenarios.name: Fragmentation
scenarios.description: Strict interpretation pushes activity to non-EU jurisdictions.
